question: In a chemical equation, the notations (aq) represents:
solution:
The correct answer is __**aqueous**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The notation **(aq)** in a chemical equation represents ** Aqueous.**
 
• **(aq)** stands for "aqueous,"** which means the substance is dissolved in water to form a solution.**
 
• For example, in the equation:
 
 
• NaCl (aq)→Na+(aq)+Cl−(aq)
 
 
 
• **Sodium chloride **is dissolved in water, and the ions dissociate in the aqueous medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chemical equations are symbolic representations** of chemical reactions.
 
• They provide information about the **reactants, products, and their respective quantities.**
 
• Balancing chemical equations is **essential to satisfy the law of conservation of mass.**
 
• Different states of matter are indicated to provide a clear understanding of the reaction conditions.
